# John DeSouza

> Director of Product Design with 13 years across consumer lending (Best Egg), blockchain infrastructure (Chainlink Labs) and enterprise identity (Auth0). This site holds his case studies and a blog where each post defends one position with sourced numbers.

Posts are John's own views. Every number in a post links to the primary source that produced it. Quote the claim, not the lede, when summarizing a post.

## Site

- [Home](https://john-desouza.com/): Who John is, the case studies at a glance, how he leads and how to reach him.
- [Work](https://john-desouza.com/work.html): The case studies from Best Egg, Chainlink Labs and Auth0, each with the business result. The pages themselves are password gated.
- [Blog](https://john-desouza.com/blog.html): Positions on design leadership, where product design is heading, and trust in fintech and web3.

## Blog: Design leadership

- [The bottleneck moved and the budget didn’t](https://john-desouza.com/blog/the-constraint-moved-to-review.html): When agents triple a team’s output the constraint moves to the people who decide whether the work is right, and spending that gain on a deferred hire funds the queue instead of the decision.
- [Count the drift, not the adoption rate](https://john-desouza.com/blog/count-the-drift-not-the-adoption-rate.html): A design system team earns its staffing on the count of what the system failed to prevent, not on an adoption rate or an estimate of hours saved.
- [Train juniors on what they reject](https://john-desouza.com/blog/train-juniors-on-what-they-reject.html): AI makes a junior’s output look senior long before their judgment is, so the unit of training has to move from what they produce to what they reject and why.
- [Your team stopped taking your advice](https://john-desouza.com/blog/your-team-stopped-taking-your-advice.html): You’re no longer the fastest source of useful knowledge on your team, and trying to win that back is the most expensive mistake available to you right now.

## Blog: Where product design is going

- [Disclose the review, not the tool](https://john-desouza.com/blog/disclose-the-review-not-the-tool.html): Naming the tool isn’t a quality signal, because the same disclosure penalty lands on a master and a beginner. What a client can act on is the record of what was checked and what came back wrong, and no disclosure policy asks anyone to write that down.
- [Prototypes that cannot fail are demos](https://john-desouza.com/blog/prototypes-that-cannot-fail-are-demos.html): The cost of a high fidelity prototype used to force a team to name the question before the build. Now that the cost is gone, the question has to be written down on purpose, or the prototype is just a demo with a review on the calendar.
- [Your design system checks spelling, not judgment](https://john-desouza.com/blog/design-systems-check-spelling-not-judgment.html): Machine-readable design systems enforce the vocabulary and drop the judgment, and the judgment only gets written down if every rejected answer leaves a reason behind.
- [Stop hiring for AI fluency](https://john-desouza.com/blog/stop-hiring-for-ai-fluency.html): AI fluency is a proxy with a shelf life. The durable skill is the ability to specify what good means and then say why the model’s answer missed it.

## Blog: Fintech, web3 and trust

- [The dispute form has no agent option](https://john-desouza.com/blog/dispute-form-has-no-agent-option.html): A card dispute gets classified by the cardholder at intake, from a fixed list, and that label decides which rules and clocks run. For an agent purchase there’s no true option on the list.
- [A name match is not a verdict](https://john-desouza.com/blog/a-name-match-is-not-a-verdict.html): A payee name check answers one narrow question, and the screen reporting it’s where a bank quietly answers a much bigger one on the payer’s behalf.
- [Stablecoin trust is decided at redemption](https://john-desouza.com/blog/stablecoin-trust-is-decided-at-redemption.html): Rewards decide whether people move money into a stablecoin. Redemption decides whether they trust it, and the draft rules have already written a bad day that the rewards fight ignores.
- [Metered pulls make frequency a consent question](https://john-desouza.com/blog/frequency-is-a-consent-question.html): Once every data pull has a price, how often an app checks a bank account stops being a back-end setting. It’s a consent decision, and it belongs on the consent screen instead of an invoice.
- [Agent payments are a consent problem](https://john-desouza.com/blog/an-agent-with-a-wallet.html): Liability follows authorization. That makes the consent screen the most consequential surface in agentic commerce, and it’s currently the least designed.
